classification.difficultyReason: Apply the specified vertical shifts to the familiar square-root curve, retaining its shape and moving its endpoint to (0,k).

content.prompt: On the same set of axes, sketch the graphs of $y=\sqrt{x}+k$ for $k=-2,-1,0,1,2$.

answer.short: Five square root curves with endpoints $(0,-2)$, $(0,-1)$, $(0,0)$, $(0,1)$ and $(0,2)$, respectively.
answer.worked: Translate $y=\sqrt{x}$ vertically by $k$ units. Each curve starts at $(0,k)$ and passes through $(1,1+k)$, $(4,2+k)$ and $(9,3+k)$. Draw the five increasing square root curves on the same axes and label each value of $k$.

spec.sourceRegion: 21D question 3; teacher PDF page 34, Section D question 3
spec.description: Five increasing square root curves on one coordinate system, vertically translated by k=-2,-1,0,1,2. Labels identify each curve; source blue is replaced by ordinary black.
spec.mathematics: For each k, x=t^2 and y=t+k for t>=0. Endpoints are (0,k); curves continue to the right beyond the displayed window.
